podcast.title: Britpop's "First Couple"
podcast.body: While in Elastica, Justine Frischmann had a relationship with Damon Albarn of Blur, and together they were considered the "first couple of the whole Britpop scene." "Justine hooked up with Damon Albart of Blur and together acted as the first couple of the whole Britpop scene."

podcast.title: Family and Personal Life
podcast.body: Justine Frischmann's father was a prominent architect, and she herself studied architecture before pursuing music. She is married to meteorologist Professor Ian Faluña and lives in San Francisco. "Her dad was a big architect and she studied architecture for a while before bailing for a career in music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Music Artistic and Academic Pursuits
podcast.body: After Elastica's breakup, Frischmann maintained a connection to music by helping her former roommate MIA develop her career. She also hosted two architecture series for the BBC, a subject she had studied previously. In 2005, she moved to Colorado to enroll in a master's program in visual arts at a Buddhist-inspired university, eventually becoming an acclaimed painter in San Francisco. "In 2005 she moved to Colorado, where she enrolled in a master's program in a small Buddhist inspired university to learn everything she could about visual arts."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Privacy in America
podcast.body: Frischmann enjoyed living in the United States because no one recognized her, offering a stark contrast to the UK where her personal life was often scrutinized. She decided to stay in America for this reason. "No one knew who she was and unlike the UK, there wasn't someone always around digging into her personal life."

xref.title: Admission of Influence and Theft
xref.body: Justine Frischmann, the leader of Elastica, openly "admitted to being such a big fan" of Wire that she "deliberately nicks some of Three Girl Rumba for one of her songs," leading to royalties from Elastica's first album being awarded to Wire. Another song, "Waking Up," also led to a portion of the album's royalties being awarded to The Stranglers for similarity to their song "No More Heroes," categorizing it as "well-intentioned theft." "In fact, she admitted to being such a big fan that she deliberately nicks some of Three Girl Rumba for one of her songs, you know, as sort of a tribute or something."

xref.body: Drug use was an even more severe issue for Elastica than Oasis, with most of the band, including leader Justine Frischmann, developing "heavy heroin habits" that prevented them from being able to write a second album. xref.title: Justine Frischmann's Post-Elastica Career
xref.body: After Elastica disbanded, Justine Frischmann collaborated with MIA, co-writing songs and achieving a hit. She also worked in television, married a professor of atmospheric science at the University of California Davis, and now works as a visual artist in San Francisco. "Justine wrote some songs with MIA and had a hit with her. She did a little TV and then she married a professor of atmospheric science at the University of California Davis."
